etymology: Phono-semantic: 是 (phonetic ダイ) + 頁 'head' — what stands at the head of a text: its title, its topic.
mnemonic: The heading at the top of the page, big letters, first thing your head meets — ダイ. 宿題 is the topic that follows you home; 問題 the one that fights back.

etymology: Compound: arrow (矢) + 豆 'stemmed vessel' — the ancients measured small lengths against arrows and cups: short.
mnemonic: Measured against a single arrow, it doesn't even reach the cup: short — みじかい. 短い夏: a summer one arrow long.

etymology: Variant of 著 'to attach': clothing attached to the body — to wear; a traveler attached to the destination — to arrive.
mnemonic: Pull the wool sweater down past your eye (目): it's on — きる. The same 'sticking' gets the train to the platform: 到着.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 主 (phonetic チュウ) — water poured in a steady stream; attention poured onto a point.
mnemonic: The master (主) tips the jug and the water threads down in one line — そそぐ. 注意: pour your mind the same way, without splashing.

etymology: Phono-semantic (simplified from 轉): cart (車) + 云 (from the phonetic 專) — wheels going around: to revolve, roll, tumble.
mnemonic: Cartwheels spinning till the spokes blur into clouds (云) — ころぶ, テン. 運転 is keeping the spin on the road; 自転車 is the spin you pedal.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 者 (phonetic ト) + city wall (阝) — the city of cities, seat of the court: the metropolis. 東京都 wears it today.
mnemonic: Everyone (者) plus walls: the city everybody moved to — みやこ, ト. 都合 is metropolitan scheduling: 'when the big city of my life allows'.

etymology: Compound: under a roof (广), a hand (又) measuring in spans — a unit of measure: degree, and each 'take' of an action: once, twice.
mnemonic: A hand ticking off spans on the workshop wall: one notch, one degree, one time — ド. 今度 is 'this next notch'; 温度 the notches of heat.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 重 'heavy' (phonetic ドウ) + 力 'strength' — muscle set against a heavy load until it shifts: to move.
mnemonic: Put strength (力) against the heaviest sack (重) and it finally budges — うごく. 動物 are 'the moving things'; 自動 is the sack moving itself.

etymology: Simplified from 發: feet planted apart (癶) and a bow releasing — the arrow leaves: to discharge, depart, emit.
mnemonic: Stance set, string loosed: whatever it was, it's launched — ハツ. Trains 出発, ideas 発明, words 発音 — all arrows off this one bow.

etymology: Phono-semantic: the sickbed radical (疒 — a person laid on a slanted cot) + 丙 (phonetic ビョウ/ヘイ): laid up: illness.
mnemonic: Flat on the tilted cot with a C-grade (丙) fever chart — びょうき. Everything under the 疒 roof is some way of feeling awful; 病院 is where the cots line up.

etymology: Compound ideograph: three boxes/mouths stacked — wares piled for inspection; many mouths judging them gives 'quality, refinement'.
mnemonic: Three crates stacked in the shop window — しな. 品物 are the crates; 上品 is how neatly they're stacked.

etymology: Originally 'to make submit / to attach to one's service' (a hand pressing a kneeling figure); clothing is what attaches to the body — dress, and 'a dose' of tea or medicine.
mnemonic: The body (月) fitted into its uniform until it behaves — フク. 洋服, 制服: cloth that tells the flesh who's in charge today.

etymology: Phono-semantic: ox (牛) + 勿 'streamers of many colors' (phonetic ブツ/モツ) — oxen of every color: things of every kind, the physical 'thing'.
mnemonic: A cow walking through fluttering ribbons: cargo of every color — もの. 買い物, 食べ物, 飲み物: name the verb, 物 makes it stuff.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 免 (phonetic ベン; originally a birth — the ultimate strain) + 力 'strength' — straining with everything one has: exertion.
mnemonic: Pushing with all your strength toward the escape hatch (免) — ベン. 勉強 is exactly that feeling, applied to a textbook.

etymology: Phono-semantic: mouth (口) + 未 'not yet' (phonetic ミ) — what the mouth knows before words do: taste, flavor.
mnemonic: The tongue meets something it can't name yet (未): pure flavor — あじ. 意味 is the same tasting done by the mind: meaning.

etymology: Phono-semantic: gate (門, phonetic モン) + mouth (口) — a mouth at the gate, calling in: to ask, to inquire.
mnemonic: Knock-knock at the gate: 'Anyone home?' — とう. Every 問題 starts as a mouth at a closed door.

etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 楽 'comfort, ease' (phonetic ヤク) — the herb that restores ease: medicine.
mnemonic: The plant (艹) that puts the music (楽) back in you — くすり. The 薬局 shelves are rows of bottled comfort.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a hand (𠂇) holding meat (月) — having something in hand: to possess, to exist.
mnemonic: A fist closed around tonight's dinner: ownership at its most primal — ある, ユウ. 有名: possessed of a name everyone holds.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 羊 'sheep' (phonetic ヨウ) — waters vast as drifting flocks: the open ocean; and what came across it: the West.
mnemonic: Whitecaps like a million sheep grazing to the horizon — ヨウ. Cross that flock and you reach 洋服, 洋食, 洋楽: the sheep-water world.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a banner with people marching beneath it — originally a military column of five hundred; the column on the move became the journey.
mnemonic: Pack behind the flag and start walking — たび. 旅行 keeps the ancient column alive: everyone still follows the tour guide's little banner.

etymology: Oracle-bone form shows a person carrying a tool — 'taking (something) as means': by, with, from a given point (以上, 以下).
mnemonic: Grab the tool and the boundary line moves with it — イ. Set the marker: 三つ以上, everything from three up; 以外, everything the tool didn't touch.

etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 央 'center' (phonetic エイ) — the central blossom, the finest flower: outstanding; chosen to transcribe 'England' (英国).
mnemonic: The one flower standing dead-center of the field, taller than the rest — エイ. It lent its brilliance to a whole language: 英語.

etymology: Compound ideograph: a brush (聿) drafting plans along a long stride (廴) — pacing out the site, plans in hand: to build, to erect.
mnemonic: Blueprint in one hand, long strides across the empty lot — たてる. A 建物 is a drawing that learned to stand.

etymology: Phono-semantic: horse (馬) + a phonetic (僉, ケン) — testing horses before buying them: verification by trial.
mnemonic: Ride the horse around the yard before you pay: that ride is the test — ケン. 試験 and 経験: exams and experience, both just laps on the horse.

etymology: Compound ideograph: woman (女) + child (子) — a mother with her child: affection itself; good, beloved.
mnemonic: Mother and child leaning into each other: the warmest picture the script owns — すき. 大好き stacks 'big' on top and means it.

etymology: Phono-semantic: plants (艹) + 采 'a hand picking from a tree' (phonetic サイ) — greens gathered by hand: vegetables, side dishes.
mnemonic: A hand in the greens, picking dinner leaf by leaf — な, サイ. 野菜: the pickings of the open field.

etymology: Compound: a phonetic top (产) over 生 'life' — life brought forth: to bear, to produce; hence products and property.
mnemonic: Under the overhang, new life (生) arrives — うむ. Farms 生産 their crops, mothers 出産, and the 産 on souvenir boxes means 'born here': 北海道産.

etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 式 'set form, ceremony' (phonetic シ) — putting performance against the set form: to test, to try.
mnemonic: Read the standard aloud (言), then try to match it (式) — ためす. 試験 measures the gap; 試着 is the fitting-room version.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 昔 'long ago' (phonetic シャク) — a person trading on old ties: to borrow.
mnemonic: 'Remember old times (昔)? So… could I borrow it?' — かりる. Debts age like the kanji says: from yesterday's favor to ancient history.

etymology: Phono-semantic: words (言) + 兌 'to loosen, exchange' (phonetic セツ) — words that unravel a knot: to explain; a theory.
mnemonic: Talk (言) until the tangled thing comes loose (兌) — セツ. 説明 is untying in public; a 小説 unties a whole life, slowly.

etymology: Phono-semantic: person (亻) + 氐 'base, bottom' (phonetic テイ) — a person down at the base line: low.
mnemonic: Someone crouched at the foundation line, head below the fence — ひくい. Low prices, low voices, low ceilings: all down at 氐.

etymology: A kokuji — a kanji invented in Japan: person (亻) + 動 'move' — a person in motion: to work. China later borrowed it back.
mnemonic: A person set in motion and kept there: work — はたらく. Japan needed a kanji for it badly enough to build one from scratch.

etymology: Phono-semantic: ox (牛) + 寺 'temple' (phonetic トク) — the bull chosen for the temple sacrifice: singled out, special.
mnemonic: Of the whole herd, one bull gets the temple ribbon — トク. 特別, 特急: whatever wears the ribbon skips the line.

etymology: Phono-semantic: food (飠) + 反 'turn over' (phonetic ハン) — rice turned in the pot as it steams: cooked rice, the meal itself.
mnemonic: Fold the rice over once more before serving — ごはん. In Japanese, 'meal' and 'rice' are the same word, and this kanji is why.

etymology: Origin debated — a flower calyx, or a bird beating upward and never arriving. Pure negation since the oracle bones: un-, non-, not.
mnemonic: A bird flapping at the underside of the sky, never getting through — フ. Stick it on anything and the thing fails: 不便, 不安, 不可能.

etymology: Compound ideograph: flesh parted from the bone with a blade (刂) — to divide cleanly: separate, distinct, another.
mnemonic: One clean stroke of the cleaver and it's two things now — わかれる, ベツ. 別々に: 'separately, please' — the check gets the blade too.

etymology: Compound: person (亻) + 更 'change, renew' — a person smoothing things over for others: convenience; the courier who makes distance convenient: the post.
mnemonic: The fixer who rearranges (更) everything until it's easy — ベン; and the mail (ビン) that spares you the trip. 便利: life with the fixer on call.

etymology: Grim origin: an eye pierced by a needle — the blinded captives of early states, hence 'the subjects, the common people'. The meaning softened into 'the people, the nation'.
mnemonic: The masses packed under one low roof-stroke, anonymous by design — ミン. 国民, 市民: the crowd every government answers to (eventually).

etymology: Compound ideograph: rice (米) + measuring ladle (斗) — grain measured out: materials, provisions, and the measured price: fee.
mnemonic: Scoop the rice, level it, name the price — リョウ. 料理 measures ingredients; 料金 measures your wallet.

etymology: Compound: two axes (斤斤) over money (貝) — goods pledged against a loan, weighed at their true worth: substance, quality; a question probing that worth (質問).
mnemonic: The pawnbroker sets two axes on the counter and weighs your treasure's real worth — シツ. 質問 does the same to a claim: 'what's underneath?'

etymology: Phono-semantic: 代 'substitute' (phonetic タイ) + money (貝) — money handed over in place of trust: to lend.
mnemonic: Your cash steps in as a substitute (代) in someone else's pocket — かす. The pair to remember: 貸す lends out, 借りる borrows in.

etymology: Phono-semantic: 尚 'lofty, esteemed' (phonetic ドウ) + earth (土) — a raised earthen platform for assembly: the hall.
mnemonic: A packed dirt stage with a proud roof: the town's gathering hall — ドウ. 食堂 is the hall that smells best.

etymology: Phono-semantic: sun (日) + 央 'center' (phonetic エイ) — light catching the center of a surface: to reflect; thrown on a screen: to project.
mnemonic: Sunlight striking dead center on the water: the world doubled — うつる. A 映画 is that trick industrialized: light, centered, forty feet tall.

etymology: Compound ideograph: grain (禾) + 厶 'hooked toward oneself' — grain raked into one's own pile: private; and the politest word for the self: I.
mnemonic: An arm curling the harvest toward its own chest: mine — わたし. The public gets 公, you keep 私: 私立, private; 私, me.

etymology: Phono-semantic: water (氵) + 先 (phonetic セン — whose old sense includes the foot going ahead) — the traveler washing feet first at the door: to wash.
mnemonic: Water over the feet before (先) stepping inside: the original welcome — あらう. 洗濯 extended the courtesy to your socks.
